overview.workflow: Begin with Fleet Health, Portfolio PR, Availability and Revenue at Risk. Compare sites in the availability and performance views, then use Maintenance Mix to determine whether the portfolio is operating proactively or reacting to failures. Open the relevant maintenance, loss, site or commercial screen for the exception that explains the portfolio result.
overview.interpret: Availability measures whether equipment was capable of operating; Performance Ratio measures how efficiently available solar resource was converted into energy. A site can therefore have high availability but weak PR because of soiling, clipping, thermal derating or sensor/data issues. Maintenance Mix percentages classify work orders and do not equal fleet-health or availability percentages.
overview.data: Portfolio KPIs aggregate plant registry, generation, irradiance, availability, work-order, asset-health, loss and commercial assumptions. Site identifiers and reporting periods must align across those datasets; otherwise fleet totals and rankings can be misleading.
overview.decisions: Which sites need executive attention? Is underperformance caused by downtime, conversion loss or maintenance backlog? How much revenue is exposed? Is the maintenance strategy sufficiently proactive? Which screen should be opened next?
overview.cautions: Do not rank sites solely on absolute MWh because plant capacities differ. Use normalised measures such as PR, availability, loss rate and revenue at risk. Confirm that irradiance and meter data are complete before treating a PR decline as an equipment problem.
overview.related: Site Performance for plant-level diagnosis; Loss Intelligence for energy-loss causes; Work Order Intelligence for action queues; Commercial & PPA for revenue consequences.

aivision.workflow: Review the inspection backlog and material findings first. Filter by plant, asset class, defect type, severity and confidence. Open a finding to compare the image evidence, affected component, estimated energy impact and recommended action before creating or prioritising a work order.
aivision.interpret: Detection confidence describes how strongly the computer-vision model recognises the visual pattern; severity describes likely operational consequence. A high-confidence low-severity finding may be less urgent than a moderate-confidence defect with safety or generation impact. Production-loss estimates depend on affected area, asset rating and persistence.
aivision.data: Uses drone, thermography, electroluminescence or field-inspection records, image metadata, plant/asset master data and defect taxonomy. Image timestamp, geolocation, asset mapping and inspection method are essential for traceability.
aivision.decisions: Which visual findings require immediate isolation, reinspection or maintenance? Which defects are recurring by module, string, tracker or inverter? What work should be bundled into the next field visit? Which finding supports a warranty claim?
aivision.cautions: Glare, shadow, dust, camera angle, weather and image quality can create false positives. Thermal anomalies should be interpreted with irradiance and load conditions. Do not approve component replacement from image classification alone when electrical verification is required.
aivision.related: Event & Root Cause Intelligence for correlated evidence; Warranty Recovery for OEM claims; Work Order Intelligence for execution; Asset Relationship Intelligence for connected defects and assets.

workorderintelligence.workflow: Use the command queue to identify critical, overdue, SLA-at-risk and ready-to-schedule work. Open the work-order record to review asset risk, expected production loss, recommended action, parts and permit readiness, then route through approval, crew scheduling and ERP/EAM synchronisation.
workorderintelligence.interpret: AI priority combines consequence, likelihood, urgency, asset criticality, expected loss and readiness; it is different from the ERP priority entered manually. Ready to Schedule means required approvals and prerequisites are satisfied. ERP/EAM Pending indicates a transaction has not yet been acknowledged by the system of record.
workorderintelligence.data: Combines work-order master and status history, asset condition, predicted failure, business impact, parts availability, crew constraints, permits, approvals and integration acknowledgements. Work-order IDs must remain stable across AIP and ERP/EAM.
workorderintelligence.decisions: Which job should be executed first? Which recommendations need approval or more evidence? Which work can be scheduled now? Which SLA is likely to breach? Which transaction failed to reach ERP/EAM?
workorderintelligence.cautions: A high AI score does not override safety procedures, outage coordination or statutory permits. Avoid closing work orders without failure code, action taken, parts used, actual duration and outcome; incomplete closure weakens Maintenance Learning.
workorderintelligence.related: Approval & Governance for authorisation; Crew Planning & Scheduling; Spares Planning; Maintenance Learning; Enterprise Integration.

corrective.workflow: Review active failures by severity, age, downtime and production loss. Confirm the failed asset and symptom, check diagnosis and parts availability, then create or advance the corrective work order through safe isolation, repair, testing and closure.
corrective.interpret: Corrective backlog is reactive work after a fault or functional failure. MTTR measures restoration duration, while repeat failure indicates whether the fix was durable. Ageing matters because an apparently low-severity defect can become material if it remains unresolved.
corrective.data: Uses failure notifications, alarms, work orders, downtime, parts, labour, failure codes and restoration timestamps. Accurate failure start and return-to-service times are needed for MTTR and loss attribution.
corrective.decisions: What must be restored immediately? Can the asset operate safely in a degraded state? Which repair is temporary versus permanent? Is specialist support or OEM escalation required? Has the same failure recurred?
corrective.cautions: Do not optimise only for rapid closure; verify repair quality and recurrence. Ensure failure codes distinguish symptom, mechanism and root cause. Production loss should be separated from planned outage or grid curtailment.
corrective.related: Event & Root Cause Intelligence; Spares Planning; Crew Scheduling; Maintenance Learning; Warranty Recovery.

preventive.workflow: Review upcoming tasks by due date, statutory requirement, asset criticality and bundling opportunity. Compare planned intervals with condition and failure history, then schedule tasks with the required crew, permits and materials.
preventive.interpret: Preventive compliance measures completion against the approved schedule. Over-maintenance can increase cost and introduce human error; under-maintenance raises failure risk. The screen should therefore be used to challenge intervals, not merely chase completion percentages.
preventive.data: Uses maintenance plans, task lists, frequencies, last-completed dates, meter readings, statutory requirements, work history and asset criticality. Calendar and usage-based triggers must use consistent units.
preventive.decisions: Which tasks are due or overdue? Can work be bundled during a planned outage? Which intervals should be extended, shortened or converted to condition-based maintenance? Are statutory tasks fully covered?
preventive.cautions: A high compliance percentage can hide low-value repetitive work. Do not defer mandatory or safety-critical tasks solely because asset condition appears normal. Record inspection findings, not just completion status.
preventive.related: Adaptive Maintenance for dynamic intervals; RCM for strategy selection; Crew Scheduling; Spares Planning; Maintenance Learning.

adaptive.workflow: Inspect tasks whose recommended interval has changed because of operating conditions, degradation, climate exposure or recent outcomes. Compare the current interval, proposed interval, evidence and risk before accepting the adjustment.
adaptive.interpret: Adaptive maintenance modifies timing while preserving the maintenance objective. A shortened interval indicates rising exposure; an extended interval indicates evidence that the original frequency may be conservative. Savings should be assessed together with residual risk.
adaptive.data: Combines preventive plans, condition indicators, utilisation, weather, failure history, inspection outcomes and maintenance effectiveness. The algorithm needs enough comparable history to avoid reacting to a single noisy observation.
adaptive.decisions: Which task should be advanced or deferred? What evidence justifies the interval change? What cost or downtime is avoided? Does the proposed interval remain compliant with OEM and statutory requirements?
adaptive.cautions: Do not automatically change regulated or warranty-mandated intervals. Guard against frequent oscillation by using approval thresholds and minimum persistence rules. Review model drift when recommendations change unexpectedly.
adaptive.related: Preventive Maintenance; Predictive Maintenance; Maintenance Learning; AI Approval & Governance; AI Model Registry.

predictive.workflow: Start with assets having high failure probability, short remaining useful life or material production exposure. Review the condition trend, anomaly onset, model confidence and recommended intervention window, then decide whether to inspect, monitor or create work.
predictive.interpret: Failure probability applies to a defined horizon and failure mode; it is not lifetime certainty. Remaining Useful Life is an estimate of time or usage before a threshold. A declining health score should be interpreted alongside operating load and sensor quality.
predictive.data: Uses SCADA and historian signals, alarms, environmental conditions, asset master data, failure labels and completed maintenance outcomes. Model coverage is limited to assets and failure modes represented in the training and validation population.
predictive.decisions: Which asset is likely to fail within the planning horizon? When is the economically optimal intervention window? Which sensor or inspection should confirm the diagnosis? What production and cost can be avoided?
predictive.cautions: Sensor drift, missing data and operating-regime changes can create false alerts. Do not compare probabilities from different models without calibration. Confirm whether the model predicts a specific failure mode or only general anomaly.
predictive.related: Prescriptive Maintenance; Risk-Based Maintenance; Event & Root Cause Intelligence; AI Model Registry; Work Order Intelligence.

prescriptive.workflow: Review each recommended action with its predicted outcome, cost, downtime, parts, crew and confidence. Compare alternatives such as monitor, inspect, repair, derate or replace, then submit the selected option for approval and execution.
prescriptive.interpret: Prescriptive ranking evaluates expected value under assumptions. The highest-ranked action is not automatically mandatory; it balances risk reduction, production recovery, cost and feasibility. Confidence should reflect both diagnosis and action-effectiveness evidence.
prescriptive.data: Uses predicted failure, consequence, maintenance history, repair outcomes, resource constraints, commercial value and business rules. Cost and energy assumptions must be current for economic ranking to be meaningful.
prescriptive.decisions: What should be done, when and why? Which alternative yields the best risk-adjusted value? Is monitoring sufficient? Should the action be bundled with another outage? What evidence is required before approval?
prescriptive.cautions: Optimisation can favour short-term economics unless safety, warranty and compliance constraints are explicit. Validate recommendations for rare or unprecedented failures where outcome history is weak.
prescriptive.related: Predictive Maintenance; AI Approval & Governance; Work Order Intelligence; Maintenance Learning; Commercial & PPA.

riskbased.workflow: Rank assets and tasks using probability and consequence, then inspect the drivers behind high risk. Decide whether to reduce likelihood, reduce consequence, improve detection or accept the residual risk under an approved plan.
riskbased.interpret: Risk is generally likelihood multiplied by consequence, but the displayed score may also include detectability, exposure and confidence. High consequence with low probability can still warrant action, especially for safety, fire or major transformer events.
riskbased.data: Uses asset criticality, failure likelihood, safety/environmental consequence, generation and revenue exposure, redundancy, detectability and mitigation status. Criticality definitions must be consistent across plants.
riskbased.decisions: Which assets need intensified monitoring or maintenance? Where should inspection and spares budgets be concentrated? Which risks can be accepted, mitigated or transferred? What residual risk remains after action?
riskbased.cautions: Numeric risk scores can create false precision. Review the underlying consequence category and assumptions. Avoid allowing frequent low-impact events to crowd out rare catastrophic risks.
riskbased.related: RCM; Predictive Maintenance; Management Actions; HSE & Climate Risk; Spares Planning.

rcm.workflow: Select an asset or system, review functions and functional failures, examine failure modes and consequences, then confirm the recommended maintenance policy: condition-based, scheduled restoration, scheduled replacement, failure-finding, redesign or run-to-failure.
rcm.interpret: RCM does not maximise preventive work; it selects the technically appropriate response for each failure consequence. Run-to-failure may be valid for non-critical, detectable and low-cost failures with no safety or environmental consequence.
rcm.data: Uses asset hierarchy, function statements, failure modes, effects, criticality, detectability, maintenance tasks and historical outcomes. Good RCM depends on precise functional-failure definitions rather than generic equipment labels.
rcm.decisions: Which maintenance strategy is technically justified? Is the proposed task capable of detecting or preventing the failure? Should the design be changed? Which hidden protective functions require failure-finding?
rcm.cautions: Do not copy generic OEM task lists without consequence analysis. RCM recommendations need engineering review and periodic validation against actual failures and maintenance outcomes.
rcm.related: Preventive, Predictive and Risk-Based Maintenance; Maintenance Learning; Asset Relationship Intelligence.

opportunistic.workflow: Review planned outages, nearby crew visits and accessible asset groups to identify additional work that can be completed with minimal incremental downtime. Confirm readiness and marginal value before adding tasks to the bundle.
opportunistic.interpret: Opportunity value is the avoided future mobilisation or outage cost minus incremental labour, material and execution risk. A task is suitable only if it is ready, safe and unlikely to extend the critical path materially.
opportunistic.data: Uses outage windows, work backlog, location, task duration, crew skills, parts availability, permits, predicted risk and mobilisation cost. Accurate duration and dependency data are essential.
opportunistic.decisions: What additional work should be bundled now? Which nearby assets can be inspected? Will the added task extend outage duration? What future mobilisation or generation loss can be avoided?
opportunistic.cautions: Avoid scope creep that jeopardises the primary outage objective. Do not bundle tasks lacking permits, parts or proven duration estimates. Preserve clear work-order and cost attribution for each task.
opportunistic.related: Work Order Intelligence; Crew Scheduling; Spares Planning; Predictive Maintenance; Management Actions.

approval.workflow: Review pending recommendations and relationship proposals by consequence, confidence, evidence and segregation-of-duties requirement. Approve, reject, request more information or override with a recorded reason.
approval.interpret: Approval status indicates governance, not technical truth. An engineer-confirmed relationship has human validation; an approved action is authorised for the defined scope. Override rate and ageing can reveal process or model-quality issues.
approval.data: Uses recommendation records, evidence, model version, user role, approval history, comments and timestamps. Identity and role data must be authoritative for auditability.
approval.decisions: Is the evidence sufficient? Is the proposed action safe and economically justified? Does the approver have authority? Is an override necessary? Which approvals are delaying operational value?
approval.cautions: Avoid rubber-stamping high volumes. Enforce segregation of duties for high-consequence decisions. Overrides without structured reasons weaken audit and model-improvement processes.
approval.related: Work Order Intelligence; Asset Relationship Intelligence; AI Model Registry; Management Actions; Enterprise Integration.

maintenancelearning.workflow: Review completed interventions by failure mode and asset class. Compare repair success, actual duration, cost, recurrence and technician/part combinations. Validate the practices that should be promoted, modified or retired.
maintenancelearning.interpret: Success Rate is successful interventions divided by comparable completed interventions and is displayed as a percentage to two decimals. Recommendation Confidence reflects sample size, consistency, recency and data completeness. A high success rate based on very few cases should not be treated as a fleet standard.
maintenancelearning.data: Uses closed work orders, failure and action codes, parts, crews, planned versus actual duration/cost, post-repair monitoring and recurrence windows. Closure quality is the main determinant of learning quality.
maintenancelearning.decisions: Which repair works best for each failure mode? Which parts and skills improve first-time fix? Which practices are ineffective or cause recurrence? Should task instructions, intervals or spares policies change?
maintenancelearning.cautions: Control for differences in asset model, environment and failure severity before comparing outcomes. Exclude incomplete, temporary or incorrectly coded closures. Do not infer causality from correlation alone.
maintenancelearning.related: Corrective Maintenance; Prescriptive Maintenance; Crew Performance; Spares Planning; Asset Relationship Intelligence.

assetrelationships.workflow: Use the Explorer to trace asset, alarm, failure, climate, work-order, spare, technician, warranty and business-impact connections. Retrieve similar cases, test what-if assumptions, propose new relationships and review evidence and approvals without leaving the same screen.
assetrelationships.interpret: Relationship Strength expresses the observed or configured degree of association; Confidence expresses evidence support. Direction matters: Extreme Heat INCREASES_RISK_OF Cooling Failure is not equivalent to the reverse. Confirmed, system-derived, AI-inferred, engineer-confirmed and proposed links carry different trust levels.
assetrelationships.data: Uses Graph Entities, Graph Relationships, Graph Evidence, Graph Similar Cases, Graph Simulations and Graph Governance worksheets. Entity IDs must match exactly across sheets. Every operational relationship should carry source, validity, confidence and approval metadata.
assetrelationships.decisions: What chain connects a hazard to a business impact? Which prior cases resemble the current failure? Which part, technician or work order is connected to a successful outcome? What changes under a heat or supply disruption scenario? Which inferred relationship is ready for approval?
assetrelationships.cautions: Graph proximity does not prove causality. Simulated impacts are planning estimates. Avoid creating duplicate or contradictory links, and do not promote inferred relationships to trusted facts without evidence and authorised approval.
assetrelationships.related: Event & Root Cause Intelligence; Maintenance Learning; Warranty Recovery; Climate Intelligence; Assistant and Work Order Intelligence.

models.workflow: Review the model inventory by capability, deployment status, owner, version and performance. Open a model to inspect purpose, covered assets, input data, validation, drift, approval and screens that consume its output.
models.interpret: Technical status distinguishes development, validation, production, monitoring and retirement. Performance metrics must match the task: precision/recall for classification, error for regression, calibration for probabilities and stability for drift. A production label alone does not imply current fitness.
models.data: Uses model metadata, versions, training population, features, validation results, monitoring statistics, approvals and deployment endpoints. Link every operational output to a specific model version.
models.decisions: Which model supports this recommendation? Is it approved and monitored? Is performance degrading? Which assets or failure modes are outside coverage? Should the model be retrained, restricted or retired?
models.cautions: Do not compare unlike metrics across model types. Aggregate accuracy can hide poor performance on rare critical failures. Monitor data and concept drift after plant, firmware or operating changes.
models.related: Predictive and Prescriptive Maintenance; AI Approval & Governance; Data Management; Asset Relationship Intelligence.

spares.workflow: Review projected demand, current stock, reserved quantity, reorder point and lead time for maintenance-critical parts. Prioritise items linked to high-risk assets and near-term work, then recommend transfer, expedite, substitute or purchase.
spares.interpret: Demand is driven by approved work plus risk-adjusted predicted demand. Days of Cover equals available stock divided by expected daily consumption. Critical stockout risk depends on timing, compatibility and consequence—not quantity alone.
spares.data: Uses item master, site inventory, reservations, purchase orders, supplier lead time, compatibility, work-order BOMs and predicted failures. Units of measure and supersession rules must be clean.
spares.decisions: Which parts will constrain maintenance? Can stock be transferred between sites? Which item should be expedited? Is an alternate part technically compatible? How much working capital is tied in slow-moving stock?
spares.cautions: Do not pool incompatible revisions under one item. Lead-time averages may understate disruption risk. Confirm warranty and engineering approval before substituting parts.
spares.related: Inventory & Materials; Work Order Intelligence; Predictive Maintenance; Asset Relationship Intelligence; Enterprise Integration.

inventory.workflow: Analyse stock by availability, value, movement, ageing and service level. Investigate excess, obsolete and stockout-prone items, then balance service risk against working capital.
inventory.interpret: On-hand, available and reserved quantities are different. Inventory Days measures cover based on demand assumptions. Slow-moving does not automatically mean obsolete if the item protects a high-consequence asset.
inventory.data: Uses item and warehouse masters, receipts, issues, reservations, valuation, reorder policy, supplier and demand history. Transaction timing and unit conversion affect balances.
inventory.decisions: What inventory can be reduced safely? Which items need higher safety stock? What should be transferred, returned or disposed? Which materials are not linked to any active asset?
inventory.cautions: Avoid using historic consumption alone for rare critical spares. Validate physical stock and repairable status. Financial valuation should follow the ERP accounting method.
inventory.related: Spares Planning; Circularity; Enterprise Integration; Work Order Intelligence; Management Actions.

warrantyrecovery.workflow: Review open claim opportunities by eligibility, financial value, Days Open, evidence completeness and filing deadline. Open the opportunity to validate asset serial number, coverage, failure evidence, OEM responsibility and required documents before claim submission.
warrantyrecovery.interpret: Days Open is an integer count from opportunity identification or claim opening to the current/closure date. Recovery Potential is expected recovery potential, not guaranteed cash. OEM Exposure aggregates eligible amounts by manufacturer and can reveal systemic product issues.
warrantyrecovery.data: Uses asset serial and commissioning records, warranty terms, failure/work-order history, parts and labour cost, production loss, OEM correspondence and claim status. Coverage dates and exclusions must be authoritative.
warrantyrecovery.decisions: Which failures are warranty eligible? Which claims are ageing toward deadline? Is the evidence package complete? Which OEM has repeated exposure? What amount should be accrued or pursued?
warrantyrecovery.cautions: Do not treat technical failure as proof of OEM liability. Check exclusions, notification periods, serial coverage and maintenance obligations. Avoid double-counting insurance, liquidated damages and warranty recovery.
warrantyrecovery.related: Event & Root Cause Intelligence; AI Vision; Asset Relationship Intelligence; Corrective Maintenance; Commercial & PPA.

crewscheduling.workflow: Select ready work and compare crews by skills, certification, availability, location, cost, experience and expected first-time-fix. Place assignments on the schedule, resolve conflicts and approve dispatch.
crewscheduling.interpret: Match Score is a weighted suitability indicator. Utilisation measures committed capacity; very high utilisation can reduce emergency response resilience. First-Time-Fix and MTTR should be read together to avoid rewarding speed over quality.
crewscheduling.data: Uses workforce roster, skills, certifications, shifts, location, travel, work requirements, duration, permits and performance history. Certification expiry and availability must be current.
crewscheduling.decisions: Who is best qualified and available? Which work can be grouped geographically? Where are skill gaps or overload? Should a contractor or specialist be mobilised? Which assignments threaten SLA?
crewscheduling.cautions: AI ranking does not account for unrecorded fatigue, local conditions or supervisor judgement. Respect working-hour, travel and safety constraints. Do not schedule work lacking parts or permits.
crewscheduling.related: Work Order Intelligence; Spares Planning; Maintenance Learning; Opportunistic Maintenance; Enterprise Integration.

esgoverview.workflow: Review portfolio sustainability outcomes and exceptions across energy, emissions, water, waste, safety and climate. Identify the measure or site driving variance, then open the specialised carbon, circularity or HSE view.
esgoverview.interpret: Absolute values show total impact; intensity values normalise by MWh, capacity or another denominator. Avoided emissions are estimated against an approved baseline or grid factor and are different from Scope 1, 2 and 3 inventory emissions.
esgoverview.data: Uses generation, fuel, electricity, water, waste, safety, land/biodiversity and emission-factor data. Organisational boundary, reporting period and factor version must be controlled.
esgoverview.decisions: Which ESG indicator is off target? Is the change operational or caused by denominator movement? Which site needs intervention? What evidence supports disclosure and management action?
esgoverview.cautions: Do not mix avoided emissions with inventory reductions. Restatements may be required when boundaries or factors change. Demo values are not disclosure-ready without assurance controls.
esgoverview.related: Carbon & Water; Circularity; HSE & Climate Risk; Management Actions; Data Explorer.

carbonwater.workflow: Analyse emissions and water use by source, site, period and intensity. Trace abnormal consumption to operating conditions or maintenance activity, then create efficiency or risk actions.
carbonwater.interpret: Scope classification follows source ownership and contractual control. Carbon intensity equals emissions divided by the selected operational denominator. Water withdrawal, consumption and discharge are distinct measures.
carbonwater.data: Uses fuels, purchased electricity, refrigerants, fleet, water meters, invoices, generation and approved emission factors. Meter hierarchy and factor geography/year must be documented.
carbonwater.decisions: Where are emissions and water hotspots? Which improvement has measurable impact? Is intensity improving independently of production? Which data gaps threaten reporting quality?
carbonwater.cautions: Avoid double-counting renewable attributes and grid factors. Estimate missing data transparently. Water risk depends on basin context, not volume alone.
carbonwater.related: ESG Overview; HSE & Climate Risk; Climate Intelligence; Site Performance; Management Actions.

circularity.workflow: Review waste generation, recovery route, hazardous classification, material reuse and inventory obsolescence. Identify high-value or high-risk streams and track actions toward reuse, repair, recycling or responsible disposal.
circularity.interpret: Diversion rate is material kept from disposal through approved recovery pathways. Recycled quantity does not automatically equal circular value; reuse, refurbishment and life extension generally retain more value.
circularity.data: Uses waste manifests, vendor certificates, material issues, scrapped components, repairable spares, packaging and disposal costs. Classification and destination evidence are required.
circularity.decisions: Which materials should be repaired, reused or recycled? Which vendor route is compliant? What waste stream drives cost or risk? Can obsolete inventory be redeployed?
circularity.cautions: Do not count storage as diversion. Verify downstream treatment rather than relying only on vendor declarations. Hazardous solar components may require specific regulatory handling.
circularity.related: Inventory & Materials; ESG Overview; HSE & Climate Risk; Management Actions; Data Explorer.

hseclimate.workflow: Review incidents, near misses, leading indicators and climate-related operating hazards. Prioritise open corrective actions and sites where exposure, control weakness and consequence combine.
hseclimate.interpret: Lagging indicators describe events that occurred; leading indicators describe control performance such as inspections, training and action closure. Climate risk combines hazard, exposure and vulnerability.
hseclimate.data: Uses incident records, observations, permits, training, action logs, weather and asset/site vulnerability. Consistent severity and exposure definitions are essential.
hseclimate.decisions: Which hazard needs immediate control? Are corrective actions overdue? Which sites face elevated heat, flood, wind or fire exposure? What adaptation or emergency response is required?
hseclimate.cautions: Low incident counts can reflect under-reporting. Do not interpret climate scenario outputs as precise forecasts. Safety decisions require local procedures and competent authority.
hseclimate.related: Climate Intelligence; ESG Overview; Management Actions; Risk-Based Maintenance; Data Explorer.

integrations.workflow: Review source and interface status, data freshness, message flow and exceptions for SCADA, historian, weather, ERP/EAM and APIs. Open failed or delayed interfaces to identify ownership and remediation.
integrations.interpret: Connected does not always mean current or complete. Last refresh, latency, record count and error queue indicate operational health. ERP/EAM acknowledgement confirms transaction receipt, not necessarily successful business posting.
integrations.data: Uses connector configuration, endpoint status, mapping rules, message logs, acknowledgements and lineage metadata. Source-system identifiers and timestamp/time-zone handling must be standardised.
integrations.decisions: Which feed is stale or failing? Which business screen is affected? Is the issue connectivity, authentication, mapping or source data? Who owns remediation? Can the platform continue using cached data safely?
integrations.cautions: Never expose credentials in the UI or workbook. Retry logic must avoid duplicate transactions. Live streaming should be separated from transactional posting and governed appropriately.
integrations.related: Data Management; Data Explorer; AI Model Registry; Work Order Intelligence; Portfolio Overview.

climateintelligence.workflow: Compare hazards by site and time horizon, inspect provider consensus and asset vulnerability, then evaluate operational and adaptation implications. Link material hazards to affected assets and maintenance strategies.
climateintelligence.interpret: Hazard score reflects severity/probability of the physical event; risk also depends on exposure and vulnerability. Provider disagreement indicates uncertainty. Scenario horizons are planning views, not daily forecasts.
climateintelligence.data: Uses weather observations, climate projections, site coordinates, terrain/exposure, asset design thresholds and maintenance history. Provider, scenario and baseline period should always be visible.
climateintelligence.decisions: Which plants and assets are vulnerable to heat, flood, wind, dust, fire or water stress? What maintenance demand may increase? Which adaptation investment should be prioritised?
climateintelligence.cautions: Do not downscale beyond the source resolution without disclosure. Separate acute event risk from chronic trends. Validate adaptation choices with engineering design criteria.
climateintelligence.related: HSE & Climate Risk; Asset Relationship Intelligence; Predictive Maintenance; Site Performance; Management Actions.

dataexplorer.workflow: Select a worksheet or dataset, search/filter fields and inspect record-level values supporting the dashboards. Use it to reconcile unexpected KPIs and identify missing, malformed or duplicate data.
dataexplorer.interpret: The explorer shows source records, not necessarily calculated dashboard outputs. Field names, units, data types and key columns determine whether a sheet can populate a screen correctly.
dataexplorer.data: Covers the active synthetic, bundled Excel or uploaded workbook. Each sheet should contain stable keys, recognised headers and consistent units. Derived values may be calculated in JavaScript rather than stored directly.
dataexplorer.decisions: Which record explains the displayed KPI? Are required rows present? Which field is blank or invalid? Does the uploaded workbook match the supported schema? Is a value source-owned or calculated?
dataexplorer.cautions: Editing in the explorer, where available, should not be confused with updating the enterprise source. Large datasets may be sampled or paginated. Protect personally identifiable or commercially sensitive data.
dataexplorer.related: Data Management; Enterprise Integration; any business screen whose values are being reconciled.

datamanagement.workflow: Choose synthetic, bundled Excel or uploaded data; validate workbook sheets and headers; review import status; reset the demo when needed. Confirm the active dataset before presenting or analysing any screen.
datamanagement.interpret: A successful file read does not guarantee full screen coverage. Validation should distinguish required sheets, optional sheets, recognised aliases, row counts and rejected values. Switching datasets should refresh data without changing the active screen.
datamanagement.data: Uses the uploader schema and sheet rules embedded in the HTML. The workbook should preserve exact keys and valid numeric/date formats. Graph sheets support Asset Relationship Intelligence.
datamanagement.decisions: Is the workbook compatible? Which screens have sufficient data? What fields failed validation? Should missing values be defaulted, rejected or corrected at source?
datamanagement.cautions: Do not silently mix synthetic and uploaded records unless explicitly designed. Treat spreadsheet uploads as demonstration/integration inputs, not a replacement for governed master data. Retain a clean baseline workbook.
datamanagement.related: Data Explorer; Enterprise Integration; AI Model Registry; all data-driven screens.

executiveperformance.workflow: Review strategic performance, value delivery and major exceptions across the portfolio. Compare actuals with targets, identify causes of variance and assign executive actions with owners and dates.
executiveperformance.interpret: Executive KPIs should distinguish operational result, forecast and value at risk. Aggregation can hide site-level outliers, so every red measure should have a traceable drill-down and accountable action.
executiveperformance.data: Uses portfolio operational, maintenance, commercial, ESG and action data. Target definitions and reporting periods must be consistent with management reporting.
executiveperformance.decisions: Are portfolio outcomes on plan? What value is being lost or protected? Which issue needs cross-functional escalation? Are prior management actions delivering results?
executiveperformance.cautions: Avoid presenting modelled benefits as realised value. Reconcile management figures with finance and operations. Do not overload the screen with measures that lack clear ownership.
executiveperformance.related: Portfolio Overview; Management Actions; Commercial & PPA; ESG Overview; Site Performance.

rootcause.workflow: Select a material incident, reconstruct the chronological sequence, review ranked causes and evidence, then validate the recommended diagnostic or corrective action. Use similar events and relationship paths to distinguish recurring mechanisms from isolated symptoms.
rootcause.interpret: RCA Confidence reflects agreement and completeness of evidence, not proof. Root Cause Distribution counts findings by category. Event Reconstruction should preserve timestamp order and distinguish precursor, trigger, protection response and consequence.
rootcause.data: Uses alarms, SCADA, historian, weather, asset states, work orders, inspection and prior incidents. Clock synchronisation and asset ID mapping are essential. Excel mode should contain enough incidents to support comparison.
rootcause.decisions: What happened first? Which alarm was causal versus consequential? What failure mechanism best explains the evidence? What test or inspection will confirm it? Is the issue systemic across similar assets?
rootcause.cautions: Alarm sequence alone does not establish causation. Common-mode data failures can mimic equipment faults. Keep hypotheses visible when evidence is incomplete and record the confirmed root cause after repair.
rootcause.related: Asset Relationship Intelligence; Corrective Maintenance; Maintenance Learning; Warranty Recovery; AI Vision.

lossintelligence.workflow: Review lost energy and revenue by site, loss category, asset and time. Separate controllable technical losses from external or contractual causes, then drill into the dominant contributor.
lossintelligence.interpret: Loss should be measured against a defined expected-generation baseline. Availability loss, performance loss, curtailment, clipping and grid outage are mutually distinct categories. Revenue impact depends on tariff and settlement rules.
lossintelligence.data: Uses meter generation, irradiance, expected-generation model, outage/event records, curtailment, equipment derating and commercial rates. Baseline model quality determines attribution quality.
lossintelligence.decisions: Where is the largest recoverable loss? Is the cause equipment, soiling, grid, weather or commercial restriction? What action has the best value? Which losses are recurring?
lossintelligence.cautions: Avoid attributing weather variance as technical loss. Prevent double counting across overlapping events. Confirm whether revenue impact is gross, net of deemed generation or subject to PPA compensation.
lossintelligence.related: Portfolio Overview; Site Performance; Event & Root Cause Intelligence; Commercial & PPA; Work Order Intelligence.

siteperformance.workflow: Select a plant and compare PR, availability, generation, losses and asset exceptions over the chosen period. Identify whether the issue is plant-wide or concentrated in a block, inverter, tracker or string.
siteperformance.interpret: PR normalises for solar resource; availability measures capability; generation is absolute output. Compare against site design, season and peer plants with caution. A weak site rank should be explained by specific loss categories.
siteperformance.data: Uses plant registry, capacity, generation, irradiance, availability, alarms, weather and loss attribution. Meter boundaries and time alignment must be consistent.
siteperformance.decisions: Why is this plant underperforming? Which subsystem drives the gap? Is the issue persistent or temporary? Which maintenance or operating action is justified?
siteperformance.cautions: Do not compare sites with different technologies, climates or commissioning stages without normalisation. Check irradiance sensor health before diagnosing low PR.
siteperformance.related: Portfolio Overview; Loss Intelligence; Climate Intelligence; Event & Root Cause Intelligence; Commercial & PPA.

commercialppa.workflow: Review contracted generation, actual delivery, tariff, availability obligations, shortfall, penalties and revenue exposure. Trace material deviations to operational causes and management actions.
commercialppa.interpret: Technical generation loss and commercial revenue loss are related but not identical. PPA clauses may include deemed generation, grid exclusions, availability bands, liquidated damages or reconciliation rules.
commercialppa.data: Uses PPA master, tariff schedules, contracted/declared generation, meters, outage classification, invoices and settlement records. Effective dates and contract versions must be governed.
commercialppa.decisions: Is the plant meeting contractual obligations? What shortfall is compensable or excluded? Which operational issue threatens revenue? What amount should be forecast, accrued or disputed?
commercialppa.cautions: Do not use simplified demo tariff assumptions for financial reporting. Avoid double counting warranty recovery, insurance and PPA compensation. Confirm legal interpretation of contract clauses.
commercialppa.related: Loss Intelligence; Site Performance; Warranty Recovery; Executive Performance; Management Actions.

managementactions.workflow: Review open strategic and operational actions by priority, owner, due date, value/risk and dependency. Update status, escalate overdue items and close only when evidence of outcome is recorded.
managementactions.interpret: Action count is not performance; focus on material value, ageing and closure quality. An action can be complete operationally but still awaiting value verification or governance closure.
managementactions.data: Uses action records generated from executive, maintenance, commercial, ESG and risk screens. Every action should have source issue, accountable owner, due date, status and expected outcome.
managementactions.decisions: What needs leadership intervention? Which action is overdue or blocked? Who owns the dependency? Has the intended risk reduction or value been realised?
managementactions.cautions: Avoid duplicating transactional work orders. Management actions should capture decisions and cross-functional commitments. Do not close actions based only on activity completion without outcome evidence.
managementactions.related: Executive Performance; Portfolio Overview; Commercial & PPA; ESG Overview; AI Approval & Governance.
